rubric.why: Identifies metals and the electrons they lose.
rubric.description: Metals lose their outer electrons easily.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals lose outer electrons easily.

rubric.why: Identifies non-metals and the electrons they gain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-metals gain electrons easily.

modelAnswer: Metals lose their outer electrons easily, while non-metals gain electrons easily.

rubric.why: Names a valid example and identifies its crystalline form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming diamond as a crystalline solid.

rubric.why: Identifies the atoms and the type of bonds between them.
rubric.description: Carbon atoms are joined by covalent bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that carbon atoms are joined by covalent bonds.

modelAnswer: Diamond is a crystalline solid in which carbon atoms are joined by covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Recognises the bond as a covalent bond.
rubric.description: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a coordinate covalent bond as covalent.

rubric.why: States how the bond behaves after formation.
rubric.description: After it is formed, it behaves like an ordinary covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that, once formed, it behaves like an ordinary covalent bond.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond. After it is formed, it behaves like an ordinary covalent bond.

rubric.why: Identifies the process and the material involved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals conduct heat.

rubric.why: Gives the reason for heat conduction in metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metals contain freely moving electrons.

modelAnswer: Metals conduct heat because they contain freely moving electrons.

rubric.why: Identifies the strong intermolecular attraction between HF molecules, including hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Strong intermolecular forces, including hydrogen bonding, act between HF molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that strong intermolecular forces, including hydrogen bonding, act between HF molecules.

rubric.why: Compares the weaker forces between HCl molecules and relates the difference to the states of HF and HCl.
rubric.description: The intermolecular forces between HCl molecules are weaker, so HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas at room temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl has weaker intermolecular forces, so HF is liquid and HCl is gas at room temperature.

modelAnswer: Strong intermolecular forces, including hydrogen bonding, act between HF molecules. The intermolecular forces between HCl molecules are weaker, so HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas at room temperature.

rubric.why: Identifies the difference in polarity between covalent compounds and water.
rubric.description: Covalent compounds are generally non-polar, whereas water is polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds are generally non-polar while water is polar.

rubric.why: States the consequence of the polarity difference.
rubric.description: Covalent compounds usually do not dissolve in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds usually do not dissolve in water.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds are generally non-polar, whereas water is polar. Therefore, covalent compounds usually do not dissolve in water.
